hints: Every path moves down-right by one step and collects one character from each visited cell.
At each diagonal position, choices determine which character can be the next character of a lexicographically smallest path.
Keep only frontier cells that share the smallest prefix found so far; discard larger-prefix routes.
analogy: At each step, keep the currently earliest alphabetic next letter and forget paths that already have a worse prefix.
example: On a 2x2 grid with top row A,B and bottom row A,C, the two paths spell AAC and ABC; choose AAC.
algorithm: Process cells by anti-diagonal. From the current optimal frontier, inspect right/down successors, retain only those with the minimum character on that diagonal, and build the answer.
correctness: All candidate paths have equal length and advance one diagonal at a time; a larger next character can never be repaired by later letters, so removing it preserves the lexicographic minimum.
complexity: O(n^2) time and O(n) frontier space for an n-by-n grid.
